provenance: Builder-authored realistic prompts, informed by known corpus coverage; no expected relevance answers. Independent human labels must be collected separately. Not a random sample of reader queries.

queries.text: We sell packaged foods. Milk, wheat and electricity costs are rising together. I want an earlier example with more than one input under pressure.
We buy green coffee for retail packs. Prices have risen; which earlier coffee business faced a comparable input squeeze?
Our milk purchasing costs have fallen compared with last year. I want a dairy example that separates input prices from price cuts and profit changes.
A chocolate maker is paying more for cocoa. We are considering price increases, but demand could weaken. Are there relevant earlier situations?
We bottle drinks in plastic and aluminum containers. Packaging and road freight costs are higher together.
Imported ingredients cost more after our currency weakened, while electricity bills are rising. I need a consumer-goods comparison rather than a commodity-price chart.
A snack maker is paying more for potatoes after a poor harvest. I need an earlier potato-cost example.
We operate an airline. Jet fuel costs have risen sharply; is there a useful comparison for this business?
In mid-2011, we are assessing higher coffee input costs. Use only information published by 27 June 2011.
As of 30 April 2025, rising cocoa costs are squeezing a chocolate producer. Which earlier report could help us compare the situation?
